newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican rebels warn government not to attack.
newsitem.headline: Mexican rebels warn government not to attack.

text.p: The Mexican government would spark a civil war if it attacked any of the country's guerrilla forces, leaders of the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) said in an interview published on Sunday.

EPR leaders said the Marxist group would launch an all-out attack on the government if it tried to crush either the EPR or the mostly Indian Zapatista Army for National Liberation (EZLN) in southern Chiapas state, the Mexico City daily La Jornada reported.
EPR commander Jose Arturo told the newspaper he feared the government was resorting to a harder line in dealing with both rebel groups.
"(We saw it) with the government's (negative) answer to the Zapatistas' demands and we see it in Oaxaca and Guerrero (states) with the stepped-up repression of social activists," Jose Arturo said.
He vowed the EPR, which first appeared in June of last year in central Mexico, would come to the aid of the Zapatistas, which appeared in 1994, were they attacked.
"We would use the full extent of our firepower to stop the bloodbath with which the government is threatening the Zapatistas," Jose Arturo said.
Talks between the Zapatistas and the government broke down late last year over the issue of Indian autonomy, although there has been no new fighting between both sides.
In Oaxaca and Guerrero, two states where the EPR operates, scores of peasant farmers have been illegally arrested on suspicion of belonging to the rebel group, human rights groups have said.
